task_completion.description: The OpenBCI GUI application is open and visible on the screen.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A window titled 'OpenBCI GUI' or showing the OpenBCI interface is present.

task_completion.description: The GUI is running an active Synthetic EEG session.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Start System' or 'Stop System' button state indicates data is flowing, and the source is set to 'SYNTHETIC (BOARD)'.

task_completion.description: The agent interacts with a widget selection dropdown menu in one of the panels.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A dropdown menu is visible over one of the existing panels, showing a list of available widgets.

task_completion.description: The 'Band Power' option is selected from the widget list.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The cursor is over 'Band Power' in the menu, or the menu highlights 'Band Power' before closing.

task_completion.description: The Band Power widget is successfully loaded into one of the GUI panels.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A panel now displays the title 'Band Power' and contains a bar graph or visualization of frequency bands.

task_completion.description: The widget displays the five classic EEG frequency bands (Delta, Theta, Alpha, Beta, Gamma).
task_completion.visual_evidence: Labels for Delta, Theta, Alpha, Beta, and Gamma are visible within the Band Power widget panel.

integrity.description: The agent used the graphical user interface to change the widget rather than command-line scripts.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor moving to and clicking the widget selection menus within the OpenBCI GUI.

integrity.description: The agent did not use a terminal to force-load a configuration file to bypass the UI steps.
integrity.visual_evidence: The terminal is not the primary window used for the configuration; the GUI remains in the foreground during the setup.

integrity.description: The widget is displaying live synthetic data, not a static image or mockup.
integrity.visual_evidence: The bars in the Band Power widget show fluctuations or movement across consecutive screenshots.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The OpenBCI GUI version is v5.2.2. The 'Band Power' widget is a standard feature. Note that while the task description uses standard ranges (e.g., Alpha 8-12Hz), the GUI labels in this version specifically show: Delta (0.5-4Hz), Theta (4-8Hz), Alpha (8-13Hz), Beta (13-32Hz), and Gamma (32-100Hz). The VLM should accept these GUI-specific labels as correct.
